474 recall questions, trend-scanned. Question visible — answer out loud, then expand.

Concept: X

  1. What is it?
  2. Why does it exist?
  3. How does it work?
  4. When do I use it?
  5. When DON'T I use it?
  6. Trade-offs
  7. Alternatives / What is it compared with?
  8. Implementation
  9. Real-world example
  10. Interview questions

The three formats — don't confuse them

Format Where Trains Density Signature

Model answers 02-Game-Day/model-answers/ — one per file; / by default; all of ML-DL, Python, LLM Foundations, RAG and React (model_answer_prompt_v1; Python edition python_model_answer_prompt_v1; AI-systems edition ai_model_answer_prompt_v1 + one pillar pack each for 04–07) Delivery under follow-up 600–1,800 words/Q 🧭 Spine + staged sections + tagged follow-ups

Phrasing drills — merged away, 19 Sep 2026

The six AI-ML oral drills (jbtiq_ml, jbtiq_dl, jbtiq_agentic, jbtiq_rag, jbtiq_llm, jbtiq_nlp — 270 questions) no longer exist as separate files. Two files per pillar meant two places to look and two things to keep in sync, so each drill was folded into its recall file. Nothing was dropped: every Hint, Recall point, One-liner:, follow-up and Note: link came across verbatim, and each drill's front-matter, question-mix and coverage tables live in a Appendix at the end of its destination file.

How a merged file reads now:

  • A drill question that overlapped an existing recall question was folded into that entry as a Phrasing drill block under the dropdown — spine first, then the script.
  • A drill question with no counterpart was appended in a ## ♻️ Merged from … section, numbering continuing from the end of the file, tagged with its origin, e.g. 🗣️ *(jbtiq_rag Q12 · S4 Embeddings)*.

🚨 If a bullet here explains something, it belongs in a v5.10 note. If it's a scripted answer, it belongs in a jbtiq drill. Here, bullets are keyword fragments and flows — nothing else. Test: read one dropdown; if it teaches you something, it's too long. It should only remind you.

Two-week cycle: 19 files ÷ ~1.5/day ≈ 12 days, leaving slack. Each file is ~40 questions at ~95 words — roughly 45 min spoken, 5 min skimmed. Two per day works on Blocks A–C; Blocks D–E carry design questions that need thinking time.

📡 Trend inputs — what the generator must pull in

Source: TREND-SCAN-2026-08 · scanned Aug 2026 · Agentic / RAG / LLM-serving. Read the scan file before generating any of files 05, 06, 08, 09, 12, 14. It is the trend layer the v2.1 prompt requires; without it the generator falls back to roundup-sourced questions, which is the documented v1.0 failure.

The five zero-coverage gaps → where each one lands

Nothing in POPULAR-QUESTIONS.md or any jbtiq_* file answers these. Each must appear in its target file, tagged 📝 No note yet until a learning-folder note exists.

Gap Band → File
Similarity score vs relevance score B 05-RAG.md
Retrieval abstention — when the grader refuses rather than returns a weak chunk C 05-RAG.md
NL-to-SQL at schema scale — many tables, how it degrades E 12-SQL-DATA.md
Token-limit-exceeded — runtime handling, not prevention D 08-LLM-SERVING-INFERENCE.md

Abstention is a template-ahead-of-content gap. interview_day_prompt_v2 uses grader may abstain in its own worked example, but the vault never defines or defends it. Fix the note before the question ships.

Thin topics to over-weight (🌗 — exist, but under-covered for how often they land)

  • Knowledge graphs / GraphRAG → 05-RAG.md + 14-SYSTEM-DESIGN-AI.md. Appeared in a real architect loop and in JDs. Construction cost + challenges is the angle asked.
  • "Improve the judge" — LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation and how you'd raise judge quality → 09. The second half is uncovered.
  • Cold start for a 70B model (GPU warm, model load) → 08. Existing cold start hits are all classical-ML/recsys sense.
  • Hybrid + semantic retrieval failure modes → 05. Only 2 hits vault-wide.
  • Chunk size ↔ embedding-model choice as one coupled decision → 05.
  • Input-side guardrails (adversarial/abusive queries before the LLM) → 10. Existing guardrail coverage skews output-side.
  • AI ROI / prioritising N use cases → 14 + 17. Architect-band axis, absent from the bank.

Recurring take-home pattern — worth its own note

Across named briefs (PromptLayer, Neura Dynamics, Cohere, Curling AI, GovGPT), the graded axis is citation, refusal and approval-gating — not retrieval quality or capability. Mandatory source attribution, safe out-of-scope fallbacks, PII refusal, human approval before destructive tool calls.

🎙️ The differentiator prompt

"Design a Hospital Voice Assistant — noise, privacy, latency, domain vocabulary." Real design prompt, and the one where the bank currently underperforms actual VhAIre/Deepgram experience. → 15-REAL-TIME-SYSTEMS.md.

The daily loop — Recite-Log

Added 24 Aug. Every file in this folder trains answering a question someone asked you. None of them train explaining your own system unprompted — which is the project round, the "walk me through your architecture" opener, and the whiteboard. That's a separate skill and it now has a separate mechanism.
Morning One drill — a sequence flow, an architecture diagram, or a war story. From memory, 2-minute cap. Paste recite_drill_prompt_v1 into a fresh Sonnet session; it plays an interrogator instructed not to praise, not to finish your sentences, and to push three escalating follow-ups.
Same day Hands-on the same component you drilled. Explaining and building reinforce each other only when they're about the same thing in the same window.
After 🔴 or a broken follow-up → Weak-Queue, verbatim, same day. Log the drill in Recite-Log either way.

🟢 means: under 2 minutes · survived three follow-ups · named a trade-off you rejected · gave a defensible number. Anything less is 🟡. Bluff words ("scalable", "robust", "we optimised it") cap you at 🟡 automatically.

This is the deliberate-practice counterpart to the T+1h step below: that captures fumbles from real interviews, this manufactures them on purpose beforehand.

Interview-day runbook

When Do this Time
T-24h Primary file, all 40 questions spoken out loud, marked 🟢🟡🔴 inline. Then the questions only from the secondary files. 50–70 min
T-3h Re-speak only 🟡 and 🔴 from yesterday. Do not re-read 🟢 — it feels productive and isn't. 20 min
T-2h questions across all routed files, spoken. Dropdowns closed unless you stall. 15 min
T-30m 16-PROJECT-STORIES.md — one out-loud rep of the two most likely stories. 10 min
T-15m Skim the question lines only — no dropdowns — of the single most-likely file. Then close the laptop. 3 min
T+1h Every question you were asked → into the right file tagged 📍 Seen in the wild. Every fumble → Weak-Queue verbatim, same day. 15 min

The T+1h step is the one that compounds. Everything else is revision; that step is the only thing that makes the next loop easier.

JD routing — which files for which interview

Read the JD, pick the row, read those files. Do not read all 17 before any single interview.

JD shape Primary (T-24h) Secondary (scan only)
RAG / knowledge assistant 05, 09, 14 04, 07, 13
Agentic / tool-using systems 06, 07, 10 05, 04, 14
AI platform / infra 08, 13, 14 09, 02, 12
AI-backend (Python-heavy) 01, 02, 05 12, 13, 06

Any 17 always —

Why the new row. 12-SQL-DATA.md was secondary in every row except classical ML, but the Aug 2026 scan found NL-to-SQL asked as an architect-band question ("scale it when the database has a large number of tables") and "Talk-to-Data" named directly in JDs. Any JD pairing enterprise data with LLMs routes here as primary.

Scoring & the feedback loop

Mark inline, in the file, next to the question number:

  • 🟢 fluent and survived the follow-up
  • 🟡 got there but rambled or missed a point
  • 🔴 froze

Rules:

  1. 🔴 → Weak-Queue the same day, verbatim question + where it broke down.
  2. 🔴 twice → the topic needs a full v5.10 note in the learning folder. This folder never grows depth; it points to depth.
  3. 🟢 three times across separate sessions → cut the question to keep the file under cap.
  4. A file whose Trend-scanned date is older than ~4 months is stale. Re-scan before the cycle, don't trust it.

Known gaps (highest ROI first)

  1. War-Stories.md is still a stub. Your own MOC says filling it "changes interview outcomes more than any folder move," and 16-PROJECT-STORIES.md is downstream of it. No template can write this — it needs your VhAIre / Mpulse numbers. This is the single highest-value hour of prep available to you.
  2. No real-time voice scenario note. The MOC flags it as "the biggest hole in the bank," and it's your actual differentiator. File 15 depends on it.
  3. 14-fast-api/ has one index file. File 02 will generate mostly from the web rather than from your vault — expect 📝 No note yet tags and treat them as a learning backlog.
  4. Weak-Queue.md is empty. An empty weak queue after months of prep means fumbles aren't being captured, not that there aren't any. The T+1h step above fixes this.
  5. 12-SQL-DATA.md is scoped too narrowly in your head. It was listed as a bare row and routed as secondary almost everywhere. The data layer under an AI system — NL-to-SQL, schema-scale retrieval, ingestion — is architect-band material and is being asked as such. Scope note and routing row now added above.
  6. No note defines retrieval abstention — question now exists as 05-RAG #43, but the note behind it still doesn't. Still a gap, one level up.
  7. No Python phrasing drill. JBTIQ_PY.md was retired 24 Aug (it was a second recall grid, not a drill — zero One-liner: entries against 45 in each AI-ML drill). A real jbtiq_python.md at ~350 words/question does not exist. Archived at 03-python/JBTIQ/_archive/ with a README; nothing was deleted.
  8. Saga / outbox / distributed transactions — asked at architect band in a real loop, no note in 05-java/ or 06-spring/. Same for Kafka consumer semantics (duplicate processing, offset handling on crash). Both surfaced by 03-JAVA-SPRING #35.

🔄 Source-channel correction (Aug 2026)

interview_day_prompt_v2 §Trend-sourcing rates LeetCode Discuss 🥇 ground truth. The Aug 2026 scan found otherwise for AI pillars: /discuss/search?q= silently discards the query and serves the generic feed, which is overwhelmingly DSA / SWE / compensation. No AI-role loops surfaced.

  • LeetCode Discuss → 🥉 for files 04–11, 14, 15. (Was 🥇 for the retired 16-DSA-PATTERNS.md; DSA pattern work now lives in the DSA vault and the published site.)
  • Aggregator repos → mandated first stop. alexeygrigorev/ai-engineering-field-guide (100+ sources, 51 companies, per-category question files and take-home briefs) out-produced both authenticated channels combined.
  • LinkedIn → still 🥈 and still worth running, but only via "interview experience" + role keywords without a date sort; date-sorted content search is ~90% recruiter spam.
  • Not yet attempted: Blind · Glassdoor · vendor engineering blogs · candidate Substacks. No question in the Aug scan cleared the two-independent-🥇 bar, so nothing is tagged yet — re-scan these before assigning trend tags.

Routing: jbtiq_rag → 05 · jbtiq_agentic → 06 (+3 to 07) · jbtiq_llm → 04 / 08 split by section (+1 to 07) · jbtiq_ml → 11 · jbtiq_dl → 11 with transformer core to 04 and inference/serving to 08 · jbtiq_nlp → new 17-NLP-CLASSICAL.md, the orphan's first real home. New counts: 04 45 · 05 62 · 06 46 · 08 30 · 11 72 · 18 45. Deliberately un-audited: every file except 07 is now over the 32–45 cap, near-duplicate pairs survive side by side, and the merged-in questions are still in drill density (~350 words) rather than recall density (~95). The next pass is the retirement/compression audit, file 11 first.

  • 2026-08-25 (b) — 11-ML-DL (25 Q, lean). Two pillars in one file, so the allocation is explicit rather than implied: 15 classical ML · 9 DL · 1 story, with ML weighted heavier because it's the half that decides the Classical ML in the loop round. DL here is the non-transformer half only — backprop, vanishing gradients, cross-entropy, initialisation, dropout, RNN failure modes, non-convergence triage — because transformer core lives in 04 and inference optimisation in 08. Compressed from 01-ML/ (15 sub-folders, the deepest classical coverage in the vault) plus 02-DL/01,02,05,09 and the 🔴 tier of POPULAR-QUESTIONS; both jbtiq_ml and jbtiq_dl audited. All → paths verified, zero dead links. Two honest gaps surfaced: drift / retrain decision framework has no note anywhere (#14, 📝 — 10-devOps/MLops/07-monitoring-observability/ and 08-retraining-lifecycle/ are README-only stubs, so this is a file-13 dependency too), and the pillar has never been trend-scanned — TREND-SCAN-2026-08 covered Agentic / RAG / LLM-serving only, so no tag is assigned in this file and the routing row runs on vault compression alone. 13 of 17 files exist. Block C is now half done (08, 11); 09 and 10 remain.

  • 2026-08-25 — Block C opened: 08-LLM-SERVING-INFERENCE (25 Q, lean). First file generated from the pillar-08 source triple — 02-DL/07-Inference Optimization/, 02-DL/08-AI systems & serving Architecture/, 05-LLM-Production/07 + /12 — plus the serving half of jbtiq_llm §7 and the 🔴 tier of POPULAR-QUESTIONS. All 25 → paths verified against the filesystem, zero dead links. Pillar boundaries stated in the header and enforced: eval → 09, guardrails → 10, GPU/K8s platform ops → 13, the design round → 14, voice latency → 15, model behaviour stays in 04. Two trend items landed as questions: gap #3 (token-limit-exceeded at runtime, 📝 No note yet — the question now exists, the note still doesn't) and the 70B cold-start question the scan flagged 🌗 because every vault cold start hit is classical-ML/recsys sense. 12 of 17 files exist; the AI platform / infra routing row now has its primary file.

  • 2026-08-24 (e) — 16 + 17, and the 2-week call. 16-DSA-PATTERNS written to the DSA override (1,174 words) — discovered 02-DSA-V2/00-index/sprint-10-day.md already exists: 46 problems, 10 days, subtitled "Senior Full-Stack / AI Engineer loop", low-yield patterns pre-skipped. 16 points at it rather than duplicating it, and adds what it lacked: 12 templates, complexity table, top-5 for an AI-backend loop. 16-PROJECT-STORIES scaffolded from INTERVIEW_DEFENSE + War-Stories — 9 stories, Situation/Task/Options prefilled, 33 <fill> blanks. 11 of 17 files exist. Recommendation on record: ~2 weeks to a defensible floor, applying from day 1 — pipeline lag is free prep, and the first loops are diagnostic.

  • 2026-08-24 (d) — Voice/real-time + the recite loop. 15-REAL-TIME-SYSTEMS written (25 Q, lean) — closes the gap the MOC called "the biggest hole in the bank" while it was also the strongest evidence available. Added Recite-Log and recite_drill_prompt_v1: a daily explain-out-loud drill with an adversarial interrogator prompt, a scoring rubric that treats bluff words as automatic 🟡, and a same-day hands-on pairing. 8 of 17 files exist. New top vault gap surfaced: no voice scenario note in 04-AI-ML/07-System-Designs/ — 15 #22 has nothing behind it.

  • 2026-08-24 (c) — GenAI core, lean pass. 04-LLM-FOUNDATIONS, 06-AGENTIC-AI, 07-MCP-CONTEXT-ENGINEERING at 25 Q each, / only; all backlinks verified, zero dead links. Introduced the 🟨 lean status and a "To finish this file" section per file so partial coverage is visible rather than implied. Pillar boundaries enforced deliberately: serving/eval stay out of 04, MCP stays out of 06, agent-loop mechanics stay out of 07. 7 of 17 files now exist — the AI-architect and agentic routing rows are covered for the first time.

  • 2026-08-24 (b) — Block A generated + RAG re-scanned. 01-PYTHON (44 Q), 02-FASTAPI (40 Q, 18 ), 03-JAVA-SPRING (40 Q, 19 🏢) written to v2.1; every backlink verified against the filesystem, zero dead links. 05-RAG appended not regenerated — 7 scan questions (#41–47), three dead header links fixed (00-Index/… → 02-Game-Day/), scan stamp bumped; now 47 Q, over cap by design until the retirement rule runs. JBTIQ_PY.md retired to _archive/ after merging its unique questions; its three production story anchors were recovered into War-Stories.md, which had never held them. Known gaps 6–8 added.

Added 📡 Trend inputs routing TREND-SCAN-2026-08's five zero-coverage gaps and seven thin topics to specific files, so the generator can't silently skip them. 12-SQL-DATA.md given an explicit scope note (data layer under an AI system, not query-writing) and a new Talk-to-Data / NL-to-SQL primary routing row — it was secondary everywhere and the scan found it asked at architect band. Added source-channel correction: LeetCode Discuss demoted 🥇→🥉 for AI pillars, aggregator repos promoted to mandated first stop. Known gaps 5–6 added.

docs.html:
🚨 This file is a scaffold, not a finished file

Every <fill> below is a number only you have. Situation and Task are prefilled from your vault. Action and Result are blank on purpose — I will not invent a latency figure or a cost saving for you, and neither should you in the room.

index known-gap #1 says filling these "changes interview outcomes more than any folder move." That is still true and it is still the single highest-ROI hour available to you. One hour tonight, before the first application goes out.

The rule from INTERVIEW_DEFENSE: if you cannot talk for four minutes from an entry, the bullet does not belong on the resume. Same test applies here at two minutes spoken.

What separates architect from engineer — the two rows interviewers actually probe:

  • Options — the 2–3 designs considered, and the real trade-off between them
  • Scar — what broke in production and what changed after

A story with Situation, Action and Result but no Options and no Scar reads as engineer. Every story below has both slots. Fill them.

S1 · VhAIre — the agentic AI interviewer lead with this one

S — Velocit AI, VhAIre. Agentic interview product: LangGraph, Deepgram Flux STT, GPT-4/4.1 + Groq, TTS. T — Sub-second turn-taking is the product. Above ~1 s the conversation stops feeling human. Options — monolithic LLM call per turn vs LangGraph state machine · Deepgram Flux vs Whisper streaming vs provider-native STT · GPT-4/4.1 for quality vs Groq for latency, and what routes to which. A — <fill: what you chose and the deciding factor. Which model routes to which turn type?> Mechanism to draw — mic → VAD → streaming STT → partial transcript → graph node → LLM → TTS → playback. Where is barge-in handled? What is checkpointed and why? What happens on a provider 500? R — <fill: p50 / p95 turn latency> Scar — <fill: what broke in production and what changed after>

Maps to: 15 #1 #5 #7 #10 · 06 #2 #13 · 04 #19 Likely probes: candidate interrupts mid-answer? · LLM slow — degrade or wait? · how do you stop the agent being gamed into leaking the rubric? · how do you evaluate interview quality — RAGAS, human rubric, both?

S2 · Deepgram ingest — backpressure under live audio

S — Continuous audio frames, Deepgram STT → LLM → TTS, real-time. T — Unbounded producer outpacing downstream consumers. Audio cannot be paused. Options — block the producer vs bounded queue with drop-oldest vs unbounded buffer. A — Bounded asyncio.Queue(maxsize=N); producer awaits on put() → natural throttle. <fill: what N was and how you picked it> R — <fill: dropped-frame rate, or latency delta, before → after> Scar — <fill: what you saw before the fix — OOM? drift? audible gaps?>

Maps to: 15 #16 · 01-PYTHON #31 · 02-FASTAPI #38 Likely probes: why drop rather than block? · how did you detect the backlog? · what did the user hear when it degraded?

S3 · WebRTC & TURN — real-time infrastructure

S — Real-time interview infra on WebRTC + WebSockets. T — <fill: what forced the work — relay cost? connection failures? scale?> Options — WebRTC SFU vs peer-to-peer vs plain WebSocket audio · managed (LiveKit/Daily) vs self-hosted. A — <fill: the choice and the deciding factor> Mechanism to draw — signalling path · STUN/TURN · what rides WebRTC vs what rides the WebSocket · how session state survives a reconnect. R — <fill: peak concurrent sessions ___ · total interviews ___ · relay ratio or cost/min before → after> Scar — <fill>

Maps to: 15 #11 #12 #13 #14 · 03-JAVA-SPRING #36 (resilience) Likely probes: what % of calls ended up relayed? · how did you capacity-plan? · what happens on wifi → cellular mid-call?

S4 · cv-parser OOMKill — the algorithmic one

S — cv-parser service, repeated OOMKill in production. T — Container dying under load. Diagnosed as algorithmic, not a leak — that distinction is the story. Options — raise -Xmx/memory limit vs fix the algorithm vs stream the work. A — Cartesian product in the matching path → dedup fix. <fill: how you found it — which tool? tracemalloc? heap dump?> R — <fill: memory before → after · restart frequency before → after> Scar — <fill: how long it ran undiagnosed, and what monitoring you added>

Maps to: 01-PYTHON #28 #32 · 03-JAVA-SPRING #29 Likely probes: how did you rule out a leak? · why didn't it show in staging? · what stops it recurring?

S5 · Founding engineer — platform 0 → 1 the architect story

S — Velocit AI, founding engineer. Platform from zero into production. T — <fill: what the business needed and by when> Options — <fill: the big early bets — monolith vs services? build vs buy on the AI layer? managed vs self-hosted?> A — <fill> Mechanism to draw — the service map. What services exist · what owns what data · what is synchronous vs queued · where the tenant boundary sits. R — <fill: scale reached — tenants, interviews, uptime, cost per interview> Scar — <fill: the biggest debt you knowingly took on — and why it was right at the time>

Maps to: 02-FASTAPI #35 #36 · 06 #24 · 07 #21 Likely probes: what would you redesign now? · what debt did you knowingly take and why was it correct then?

S6 · Provider-agnostic LLM integration layer

S — Multiple model providers behind one internal interface. T — Swap providers without rewriting callers; A/B a model change safely. Options — thin passthrough vs full abstraction vs per-provider adapters. A — <fill: what's in the interface — and what leaked through anyway> Mechanism — how prompts and model configs are versioned · how you A/B a model change · fallback on provider failure. R — <fill: providers supported · time to add a new one · cost or quality delta from routing> Scar — <fill: what leaked through the abstraction>

Maps to: 04 #24 · 07 #22 · 02-FASTAPI #29 Likely probes: what leaked? · how do you A/B without breaking prod? · how do you version prompt + model together?

S7 · AWS / EKS — spot instances vs live sessions

S — Owned AWS end to end: EKS via Terraform + Helm, spot instances, Argo CD. T — Infra cost vs interrupting a live interview on a spot reclaim. Genuine tension, great story. Options — on-demand throughout vs spot with drain handling vs mixed node groups by workload. A — <fill: descheduler + node-termination handler — what do they actually do during a live session? how do you drain a node with an interview in flight?> R — <fill: infra cost per interview ___ · % saved by spot ___ · sessions lost to reclaim ___> Scar — <fill>

Maps to: 15 #15 · 02-FASTAPI #30 #33 Likely probes: what's the drain window vs your longest session? · did you ever lose a live interview to a reclaim?

S8 · FastAPI domain-driven refactor

S — FastAPI service, layering had eroded. T — <fill: what the tangle was costing — change risk? test time? onboarding? an incident?> Options — incremental extraction vs big-bang rewrite vs leave it and document. A — Split into api/ · domain/ · infrastructure/, dependencies pointing inward. <fill: how you did it without stopping feature work> R — <fill — this one badly needs a number. "Cleaner" is not a result. Test runtime? PR cycle time? Defect rate?> Scar — <fill>

Maps to: 02-FASTAPI #23 #25 · 03-JAVA-SPRING #24 Likely probes: how did you avoid a freeze? · what still isn't clean? · how do you stop it eroding again?

S9 · Technical lead, 6 engineers (behavioural — every loop has one)

S — Tech lead for a team of 6. T — <fill> A — <fill: how work was split · how architecture decisions got made — did you write ADRs? · the review standard · how you handled a disagreement> R — <fill: delivery, quality, or retention outcome> Scar — <fill: a decision you made that the team pushed back on — and what you did>

Maps to: the leadership round in every senior/staff loop Likely probes: disagreement with your own manager? · how do you grow juniors? · a call you got wrong?

Which story for which prompt

They ask Lead with
"Most technically challenging project" S1 → depth via S2 or S3
"Walk me through an AI system you built end to end" S1, draw the turn
"Debug a hard production issue" S4 (or S2)
"A time you optimised for scale or cost" S7 or S3
"Design decision you'd make differently" S5 (the knowing debt)
"Disagreement / leadership" S9
"Something you're proud of" S1
Java/Spring shop S8, then S5

Rules. Two minutes, then stop and let them probe. Never open with the stack — open with the constraint. Name the option you rejected, unprompted; it is the single highest-signal sentence you can say.

Completion check

Cross these off as you fill them. Do not start applying with more than two unchecked.

  • S1 — turn latency p50/p95
  • S2 — dropped-frame or latency delta
  • S3 — concurrent sessions, relay ratio or cost/min
  • S4 — memory before → after
  • S5 — scale reached, and the knowing debt
  • S7 — cost per interview, % spot saving
  • S8 — a real number, not "cleaner"
  • Every story has an Options line and a Scar line

Drill these in Recite-Log STORY mode. A story you've never said out loud is not a story, it's a paragraph.
